scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: Compare pairs, not group names: together on both sides, or apart on both?

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: the left shows the two partitions of Example 16.1; each cell on the right is one pair, colored by its kind (first letter for $\mathcal{C}$, second for $\mathcal{P}$: together is $\mathrm{S}$, apart is $\mathrm{D}$).

scene-u01-pnew1-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew1-8.text: Example 16.1: $N=6$, the partitions differ in size

scene-u01-pnew1-40.name: text#40
scene-u01-pnew1-40.text: The only difference is $\mathbf{x}_6$: alone in $\mathcal{C}$, but grouped with $\mathbf{x}_4$ and $\mathbf{x}_5$ in $\mathcal{P}$

scene-u01-pnew1-103.name: text#103
scene-u01-pnew1-103.text: Both purple DS cells involve $\mathbf{x}_6$: the only disagreement between the partitions

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: All four indices grow with agreement, but only a random reference tells what is large

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: the left gives the four formulas with Example 16.1 values; the right shows source Example 16.2, where solid bars reject $H_0$ and dashed outlines do not.

scene-u01-pnew2-29.name: text#29
scene-u01-pnew2-29.text: Jaccard leaves out $d$, so many apart-on-both pairs cannot inflate it

scene-u01-pnew2-30.name: text#30
scene-u01-pnew2-30.text: $\hat{\Gamma}$ is the correlation of the upper triangles of two $0/1$ matrices

scene-u01-pnew2-32.name: text#32
scene-u01-pnew2-32.text: Source Example 16.2: four groups, $\rho=0.05$, increasingly spread

scene-u01-pnew2-73.name: text#73
scene-u01-pnew2-73.text: Misconception: "Rand is $0.63$, over half, so the clustering is decent."

scene-u01-pnew2-74.name: text#74
scene-u01-pnew2-74.text: (c) has almost no structure, yet $R$ is still $0.63$: the many DD pairs make $a+d$ large anyway. Compare with a random reference, not the absolute value.

scene-u01-pnew2-75.name: text#75
scene-u01-pnew2-75.text: Source: week15-v01 lecture lec15-kp02-external-indices §3 (Example 16.2 numbers from the source)

scene-u01-pnew2-76.name: text#76
scene-u01-pnew2-76.text: The four values of Example 16.1 computed by code

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: No algorithm needed: does a given grouping fit the distance structure?

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: the left colors $64$ points by the given partition; the gray histogram on the right is $\hat{\Gamma}_i$ of $100$ random labelings, green is the correct labels, orange a random assignment.

scene-u01-pnew3-76.name: text#76
scene-u01-pnew3-76.text: $Y(i,j)=1$: the two points are in different groups of $\mathcal{P}$; otherwise $0$

scene-u01-pnew3-77.name: text#77
scene-u01-pnew3-77.text: Points in different groups are usually farther apart, so correct labels give a high $\hat{\Gamma}(P,Y)$

scene-u01-pnew3-78.name: text#78
scene-u01-pnew3-78.text: $P$: squared Euclidean distance; random label hypothesis

scene-u01-pnew3-80.name: text#80
scene-u01-pnew3-80.text: Random label hypothesis: one $\hat{\Gamma}_i$ for each of $100$ random groupings

scene-u01-pnew3-105.name: text#105
scene-u01-pnew3-105.text: Correct partition $\hat{\Gamma}=0.77$, above all $100$; random grouping $\hat{\Gamma}=-0.01$, below only $70$

scene-u01-pnew3-109.name: text#109
scene-u01-pnew3-109.text: With standard deviation about $0.39$ the groups overlap heavily, so the value is smaller; but correct labels far above random and random assignment inside it agree with the source.

scene-u01-pnew3-111.text: Redrawn data and numbers computed by code [Added]
